clue.text: Pursuit of hobbyist putting a foot down about part of office?

indicators.note: about means the word for treading heavily goes around the church-service piece

parts.note: putting a foot down hard is stamping
a collect is a short prayer, part of a church office or service

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a hobbyist does when putting a foot down over a corner of the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace but is a church service, of which the collect (a short prayer) is part. 'about' wraps STAMPING round it: STAMP-COLLECT-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately, gathering postage issues, is the classic example of a hobbyist's pastime.

clue.text: Extra appointment for teacher? This could delay notification

definitions.meaning: a second job taking another class: a further teaching post
cheaper, slower mail, so a letter of notice arrives later

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders about a second job while noting that cheap mail slows news.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase as a second, class-teaching post; the second is the slower UK mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it is a further teaching job; as a fixed term it is the slower, cheaper British mail tier.

clue.text: One Bee Gee's heart of gold

indicators.note: the heart of a word is what remains once its outer letters are removed

parts.note: Maurice Gibb was one of the three Bee Gees

explanation.surface: A tribute claims one of the Bee Gees had a heart of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' strips the first and last letters from MAURICE, the name of one of the Gibb brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin aurum and describes things relating to or containing that precious yellow metal.

clue.text: Cover coming before book?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a text is a book, especially a set one

explanation.surface: A question about a dust jacket, the cover that comes before the book itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse or false reason serves as a cover for one's real motive.

clue.text: I snubbed friend after returning second letter

indicators.note: after means the rest follows the turned-round piece
returning means the word for a brief moment is read backwards

parts.note: MO is a short moment, a second ('wait a mo')

indicators.note: snubbed, like a snub nose, means cut short: the friend loses its tail

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Someone who snubbed a friend finally returns a second letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is a brief moment, as in 'wait a mo'; 'returning' turns it round, and 'snubbed' means cut short like a snub nose.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifteenth character of the Greek alphabet, the short O.

clue.text: Arm taken by much acclaimed thespian?

definitions.meaning: an arm is a weapon, here a tall archer's bow
an actor greeted with great applause may take a long, drawn-out bow

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor takes someone's arm on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a lengthy bow is what an applauded actor takes at curtain call.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall English bow was a famous medieval weapon, and arms are weapons.

clue.text: Where federal laws created a hidden problem in Colorado

indicators.note: in means the hidden-problem piece goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Col. is an abbreviation for the US state of Colorado
a pit is a hidden hazard, like a pitfall

explanation.surface: An exposé of how federal legislation caused a concealed snag in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: Colorado is abbreviated COL as well as CO; A PIT goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The building in Washington DC houses the US Congress, which makes federal legislation.

clue.text: Anxious setter will tantalise, concealing answer

indicators.note: concealing means the pieces hold the abbreviation for answer inside them

parts.note: the setter speaking says I'll, short for I will
to tease is to tantalise

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of teasing solvers by hiding the solution, making them nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks of themself as I, so 'setter will' becomes the contraction of I will; 'concealing' tucks the answer letter in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uneasy and uncomfortable is the same as being worried or nervous.

clue.text: Auf wiedersehen, literally?

parts.note: the German farewell, rendered into English, is a parting wish to the German capital; 'literally' also hints at literature

explanation.surface: A query about the literal meaning of the German farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Christopher Isherwood's 1939 novel of Weimar Berlin, later the source for Cabaret. 'Literally' doubles as 'in literature'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isherwood's book title is the English farewell to the city where the German phrase would be spoken.

clue.text: Hoax involving Russia's foremost essayist's a gem

indicators.note: involving means the hoax word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a con is a hoax or swindle

indicators.note: foremost means the opening letter of Russia is taken

parts.note: Elian means of Elia, the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A hoax involving Russia's top essayist is praised as a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia, so the adjective for that essayist serves for 'essayist's'. 'foremost' picks only the first letter of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: This red variety of chalcedony, also called carnelian, is a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Disease from India caught by traveller to the East

indicators.note: caught by means the letter for India is held inside the traveller

parts.note: Marco Polo travelled from Venice to China
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A disease brought back from India by a traveller to the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Poliomyelitis is a viral infection that can cause paralysis.

clue.text: Type of energy in doubt, given initial setback

indicators.note: the initial letter is set back, moved one place later in the word

parts.note: unclear means in doubt

explanation.surface: The future of a kind of power is in doubt after an early setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial setback' moves the first letter of UNCLEAR back one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Power released by splitting or fusing atoms is a kind of energy named for the atom's core.

clue.text: Temperature in small animal centre dips here, perhaps

parts.note: a bat is a small flying mammal

indicators.note: in means the temperature letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a hub is a centre

explanation.surface: At a small-animal centre the temperature dips here, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dips' looks like the temperature falling, but it is taking a dip, a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for bathing is where someone might take a dip, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: I'm surprised state doesn't have one

indicators.note: doesn't have means the piece for one is missing from the state

parts.note: Ohio is a US state
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to learn that a state lacks one of something.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an interjection of surprise, like 'well, well!'

clue.text: Old batting hero may prefer to open after duck between centuries

indicators.note: between means the middle pieces sit within the two centuries

parts.note: C (Roman 100) and TON (slang for 100) are both centuries

indicators.note: after means the opening letters follow the duck

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought, so O

indicators.note: to open means the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A veteran batsman would rather open the innings after a duck between hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: Denis Compton was a great England batsman of the 1940s and 50s. 'centuries' supplies two different hundreds, the Roman numeral and the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Compton was a celebrated England and Middlesex cricketer, so an old hero of batting.

clue.text: Jack behind manoeuvre to arrest current Hollywood actor?

indicators.note: behind means the sailor comes after the rest
to arrest means the manoeuvre holds the current letter

parts.note: to move pieces or troops is to manoeuvre
I is the symbol for electric current
a jack or jack tar is a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A sailor follows a plan to arrest a fashionable Hollywood actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name but is a sailor; 'current' is the physics symbol for electric current, not 'up to date'.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous film performer is the typical example of a Hollywood actor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A certain cardinal's joke

definitions.meaning: a cardinal number, the first counting number
a joke, as in 'have you heard the ... about...'

explanation.surface: A particular churchman is known for a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a prelate but is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a particular person, is the lowest counting number, and stands for a joke being told.

clue.text: Benefit from meals on wheels on a regular basis

indicators.note: on means the meals piece is placed after the regular letters
on a regular basis means every other letter of wheels is taken

parts.note: fare is food, meals

explanation.surface: Someone benefits from the meals-on-wheels service delivered regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on wheels is a UK service delivering hot food to the housebound. Alternate letters of wheels give WEL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain and the US it names state support payments, a benefit to those in need.

clue.text: Number two in team running for a long time

indicators.note: number two in means the second letter of team is taken

parts.note: a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: The team's second-in-command has been running things for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or vast span of time, often used loosely for a very long time.

clue.text: Recommended additives losing it when cooked

indicators.note: losing means the letters of it are dropped from the pool
cooked means the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food additives were recommended, provided they lose their effect in cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of 'it' out of ADDITIVES and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Counselled or suggested, both meaning recommended, as in 'well advised'.

clue.text: Runner with promise revolutionised slum area

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

indicators.note: revolutionised means the promise word is turned right round

parts.note: giving one's word is promising

explanation.surface: A runner with a promise of change transformed a poor district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: The American term for a run-down district of vagrants and down-and-outs.

clue.text: Arrogance, it's said, developing during row

indicators.note: during means the rearranged letters are placed inside the row

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: developing means the letters of said are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Arrogance, people say, emerges during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' turns SAID into ISDA, which goes into DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn or contempt is an attitude of haughty superiority, close to arrogance.

clue.text: Busy gent, husband running round in circles

indicators.note: in means the mixed letters sit inside the two circles

parts.note: each circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: running round means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A busy man and her husband are running round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantly active and on the move, idiomatically, is the same as busy.

clue.text: Oscar presumably eating cereal

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone at a meal is presumably eating

explanation.surface: Oscar is eating his breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats are a cereal, used for porridge.

clue.text: Red wine, small amount, but guy needs it

parts.note: tent is a deep-red Spanish wine
a peg is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A man wants red wine, just a little, but needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope, which needs a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope steadying a tent is fixed to the ground by one of these stakes.

clue.text: Girl has help cycling

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter of the help word goes round to the end

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A girl gets assistance with her cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida.

clue.text: Class that is wearing glasses

indicators.note: wearing means the glasses go around the abbreviation, as if worn

parts.note: specs are spectacles, glasses
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A schoolroom where everyone is wearing glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a kind or class of organisms that can interbreed.

clue.text: Seemingly rational little gap in record

indicators.note: in means the small space goes inside the record

parts.note: a table is a record of data
an en is a small space in printing

explanation.surface: Something seems rational but leaves a little gap in the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that can be defended or maintained looks reasonable on its face.

clue.text: Pop runs in front of lady

indicators.note: in means the runs letter goes inside the lady's front

parts.note: a woman's bust is at her front
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Dad runs ahead of a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of lady' looks like her initial L, but is her bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop is to break open suddenly, as a balloon does.

clue.text: Pigeon quietly flying off further from centre

indicators.note: flying off means the letter for quietly departs from the bird

parts.note: a pouter is a breed of pigeon that puffs out its crop
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pigeon quietly flies off away from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: More external, nearer the edge, is the opposite of inner.

clue.text: Timeless ruins at Palermo

indicators.note: ruins, as a verb, means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Timeless ruins are found at Palermo, in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing outside time, unaffected by it, is a formal way to say timeless.

clue.text: Making plainer group of women in press come across

indicators.note: in means the women's group goes inside the crowd

parts.note: a press of people is a throng
WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
to light on something is to come across it

explanation.surface: Women in a crowd of the press come across something that makes it clearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalists but is a crowd; the WI is Britain's Women's Institute.
explanation.definitionFit: Illuminating a matter, idiomatically, means clarifying or explaining it.
